newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The interior minister has declared he will take tough action against certain groups of workers he claims have been paid by a foreign economic rival to foment labour unrest. Sanoh Thienthong's remark comes in response to suggestions the arrest of Chin Thapplee, a labour leader, on Wednesday is an act of persecution. (BANGKOK POST)

- At least 28 workers were killed, 15 injured and eight missing after a bus plunged into a canal after bursting a tyre late on Wednesday night. Most of the 50 passengers drowned in deep, fast-flowing water after the driver lost control of the bus. The bus had been taking the workers from a factory to their homes. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Cash-strapped Bangkok Land Plc has made progress in its application to reclaim a portion of the two billion baht guarantee it deposited with the Sports Authority of Thailand (SAT) to carry on with construction of the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games sports complex. SAT board members have met at the Government House where they unofficially approve Bangkok Land's request. The final decision rests with the Cabinet. (THE NATION)

- Two out of three applicants for the new banking licences want the Bangkok of Thailand (BOT) to extend the deadline for starting operations, citing the downturn in the economy as the main reason. The government has earlier issued three new banking licences to consortia led by General Finance and Securities, MBK Properties and Development and Italian-Thai Development. The plan originally was to issue a maximum of five banking licences. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The findings of a joint research project released yesterday by Chulalongkorn University, the Industrial Finance Corp and Kasetsart University blamed successive poor governments for the country's declining international competitiveness. The study's conclusions mirror studies by international competitiveness rating agencies. The study found that the public sector has experienced the steepest decline in efficiency. (THE NATION)
